title: Hocus Pocus Lesson
subtitle: Roll it back, tap it in, flick it behind your standing leg. Taught from one tutorial video and the 3D body reconstructed from it.
sourceNote: one public tutorial clip (credit its creator before any real use), the body motion reconstructed from it, and measurements taken from that motion.

skills.name: Roll-back hocus pocus
skills.intro: Four steps in under two seconds: stop the ball under your sole, roll it back, tap it in, then flick it behind your standing leg and go. Watch the night demo at full speed, then at half speed.

notice.title: Stop it
notice.text: The ball arrives under his foot as the defender steps in.

notice.title: Roll back
notice.text: He drags it back under his body with his sole.

notice.title: Tap in
notice.text: A short tap moves it across towards his standing foot.

notice.title: Hocus pocus
notice.text: The ball foot whips behind the standing leg and sends the ball the other way.

notice.title: Exit
notice.text: He is past the defender before the defender can turn.

skills.adds: The night demo is too dark and fast to read, so the lesson breaks the move down with the tutorial and the side-on replay. In the 3D you can turn the camera behind him to see the ball foot go round the standing leg.
unsure: Which of his legs does the work. The 3D can mix up his legs when they come together over the ball, so the lesson names feet by their job.
Whether the flick uses the inside or the outside of the foot: the foot is hidden behind the standing leg.
Anything about the ball in the night demo: the tracker followed a spare ball, so it isn’t shown there. That part’s 3D is rough too (moving camera, low light).
skills.breakdownIntro: The tutorial’s four labelled steps plus the moments around them. Open one to freeze on it; play it to loop it at half speed. The overlays switch to what matters for that moment.

phases.name: Set up
phases.cue: Ball close; arrive on your standing foot.
phases.video: He walks the ball in towards the camera, keeping it within a stride.
phases.shows: His standing foot comes down at 3.90 s and stays planted for 2.8 s, through every touch that follows.
phases.why: The plant is slow and clearly visible.

phases.name: Roll back
phases.cue: Sole on top of the ball; roll it back under you.
phases.video: The sole of the ball foot sits on top of the ball and draws it back towards him.
phases.shows: The ball foot stays in touching distance of the ball while the body drops about 15 cm. His weight sits almost entirely over the standing foot.
phases.why: Weight is inferred from where the body sits between the feet.

phases.name: Tap in
phases.cue: Inside of the same foot: tap it across to your standing foot.
phases.video: Small taps with the inside of the ball foot move the ball across towards the standing foot.
phases.shows: 3 small touches by the ball foot in under a second, with the body held about 15 cm lower than standing. The standing foot doesn’t move.
phases.why: Single-camera ball depth: touches are counted when the foot comes within a few centimetres.

phases.name: Hocus pocus
phases.cue: Wrap the ball foot behind your standing leg and flick it across.
phases.video: Bent over the ball, he reaches the ball foot round behind his standing leg and sends the ball to the other side.
phases.shows: At 5.60 s his hips swing about 35° in a fifth of a second as the ball foot goes behind. He is still balanced on the standing foot.
phases.why: One camera: which leg is in front when they cross can’t be confirmed.

phases.name: Exit
phases.cue: Stand up and take it away the other way.
phases.video: He straightens up and steps off after the ball.
phases.shows: The standing foot finally lifts at 6.67 s and the body rises back to upright within about a quarter of a second.
phases.why: The camera is low and close; the step-off is partly out of frame.

phases.name: Side-on replay
phases.cue: The same pattern at speed, seen from the side.
phases.video: From the side you can see how low he gets as the ball foot goes behind the standing leg.
phases.shows: He gets about 21 cm lower than standing here, lower than in the tutorial, and his body turns about 77° as he takes it away.
phases.why: Fast movement; the body turns away from the camera.

drills.title: Sole roll on the spot
drills.how: Stand beside the ball. Put your sole on top and roll it back under you, then stop it. Keep the standing foot still the whole time.
checks: My sole stayed on top of the ball
The ball stopped beside my standing foot

drills.title: Roll and tap in
drills.how: Roll it back, then tap it across towards your standing foot with the inside of the same foot. Two or three small touches, not one big one.
checks: I stayed low over the ball
My touches were small and close
My weight stayed on the standing foot

drills.title: Behind the standing leg
drills.how: From the tap-in position, reach the ball foot round behind your standing leg and push the ball across to the other side. Go slowly until you stop clipping your own heel.
checks: My ball foot went behind my standing leg
The ball crossed to the other side

drills.title: The whole move, walking pace
drills.how: Roll, tap, hocus pocus, then stand up and take it away for three steps. Join the steps with no pause.
checks: I stood up and went the other way
I could do it at jogging speed

drills.title: Against a passive defender
drills.how: Dribble at a partner who steps in but doesn’t tackle. Stop the ball as they arrive, roll and tap, then flick it behind your leg and go past.
checks: I stopped the ball as they stepped in
The flick went past their reach

challenges.title: Where is the weight?
challenges.prompt: Frozen during the roll back. Where is his weight?
challenges.explain: The ball foot rests lightly on top of the ball while his weight stays over the standing foot; the meter sits at the standing end. That’s what frees the ball foot to roll, tap and flick.

challenges.title: Spot the hocus pocus
challenges.prompt: Tap the moment the ball foot whips behind the standing leg.
challenges.label: Now!
challenges.explain: The hips swing fastest as the foot goes behind the leg.

challenges.title: What happens next?
challenges.prompt: Frozen just after the hocus pocus. Predict the next movement.
options: He stands up and takes the ball away the other way
He rolls it back again with his sole
challenges.explain: The hocus pocus moves the ball out of the defender’s reach; the exit is where you accelerate.

challenges.title: Put the steps in order
challenges.prompt: Tap the moments in the order they happen.

limits: The night demo’s 3D is rough: the camera moves with him in low light, and the tracked ball there was a spare one, so it’s hidden.
tests: Whether learners can pick out the three touches (roll, tap, flick) at full speed after the tutorial.
